clue.text: Get the wrong idea about tailored denim perhaps

indicators.note: tailored means cut and refashioned, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone misreads what made-to-measure jeans might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailored denim' reads as a garment, but 'tailored' is the anagram signal working on both 'denim' and 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: To misunderstand something is to form a mistaken notion of it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Sum up South: Presley denied half a dozen shellfish

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word sum is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
S is the compass abbreviation for South

indicators.note: denied means deprived of, so letters are taken away from the singer's name

parts.note: Elvis Presley, the singer
six, written as the Roman numeral VI

explanation.surface: An instruction to tally things up in the South, with Elvis missing six of something, ending in seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: ELVIS without VI leaves ELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mussels are bivalve molluscs, a kind of edible shellfish; plural matches plural.

clue.text: James left note for creep

parts.note: Sid James, the British comic actor of the Carry On films
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone called James walked out and left a note for a sneaky person.
explanation.walkthrough: Sid James was a British comedy actor famous from the Carry On films.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep and to edge along furtively are the same verb sense.

clue.text: Shut up about access to field possibly causing trouble

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for shut up encloses the other piece

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means confined
a stile is steps over a fence giving access to a field; possibly marks it as an example

explanation.surface: Someone confined near a field gate may be making a nuisance of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilent in its figurative sense means annoying or troublesome, as a nuisance is.

clue.text: Engineers regularly raised limit

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the chosen letters are read upwards
regularly means taking every other letter of the word engineers

explanation.surface: Engineers steadily push up a ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of Engineers give NIER, which 'raised' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein something in is to restrain or curb it, a synonym of limit as a verb.

clue.text: Paying no attention like the proverbial chicken — using Ecstasy not the answer

indicators.note: using signals that a new letter is brought into the word
not signals the letter that is dropped to make room

parts.note: the proverbial chicken runs around headless
A is an abbreviation for answer
E is the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone careless rushes about like a headless chicken, on drugs and without answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Being heedless means taking no notice or care, the same as not attending.

clue.text: Smart new 12-inch Sony at last

parts.note: twelve inches make one foot: I (one) plus FT (foot)

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the brand name Sony

explanation.surface: A stylish new twelve-inch Sony gadget, finally.
explanation.definitionFit: Nifty and smart both mean clever or stylish in an informal way.

clue.text: Welcome appeals by a conservation group

parts.note: pleas are appeals or requests
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation body

explanation.surface: A conservation charity is glad to receive appeals.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust looks after historic houses and countryside in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Welcome as an adjective means agreeable or gladly received, a synonym.

clue.text: TV comedian's housing rent cut

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the comedian's name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Jack Dee, the British TV comedian
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A TV comedian's rent on his home has been reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Dee is a deadpan British stand-up and TV comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut text or a scene is to remove it, the same as erasing it.

clue.text: Passing criticism for punch not delivered head-on

definitions.meaning: an incidental dig or jibe made in passing
a glancing blow struck from the side

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions joined by 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an indirect critical remark and a blow landed from the side.

clue.text: Mock intermittently flawless English

indicators.note: intermittently means on and off, so alternate letters of flawless are taken

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at English that is only sometimes flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of flawless give FALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mock as an adjective means sham or imitation, a synonym of fake or untrue.

clue.text: Seedily fashionable seafront's disappearing — it's closed some of the time

definitions.text: it's closed some of the time

indicators.note: fashionable here means fashioned or shaped anew, so the letters of seedily are rearranged
disappearing means a letter vanishes from the mix

parts.note: the front of the word sea is its first letter S

explanation.surface: A seedily trendy seafront is fading away.
explanation.walkthrough: Seedily rearranged, with the S from the front of 'sea' removed, leaves the six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the flap of skin over the eye shuts in blinking and sleep.

clue.text: Spring horse race according to Spooner's pal

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: May is a spring month
a plate is a horse race with a prize

explanation.surface: A friend's version of a springtime horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: MAY PLATE with the opening M and PL swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A friend to play with, a companion; synonym of pal.

clue.text: Bill's temperature dropping, becoming more poorly

indicators.note: dropping means a letter is let fall from the word

parts.note: a bill is a poster or label, a sticker

explanation.surface: Bill's fever is falling, yet he is getting worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of ill: less well, in worse health.

clue.text: Concentrate with not very clever trick first

indicators.note: first places the trick at the start, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
dense means dim, slow-witted

explanation.surface: Focus, combined with a dim-witted piece of trickery first.
explanation.definitionFit: To concentrate a liquid or text is to reduce it into a smaller compass, a synonym.

clue.text: Concoct a résumé including number for online identity

indicators.note: including means holding a letter within
concoct means devise or make up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of a resume, accent ignored

explanation.surface: Make up a CV with a figure in it to present yourself online.
explanation.definitionFit: The handle a person logs in with is their name on the internet, their identity there.

clue.text: No vehicle backed up? Strangely true, one can tell

indicators.note: backed up in a down clue means read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: no plus car, a vehicle

indicators.note: strangely means oddly arranged, so the following letters are mixed

explanation.surface: No car reversing? Oddly enough, it's true, someone can vouch for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one can tell' means one who tells stories, not someone able to judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled storyteller, someone who tells tales.

clue.text: Puzzle unusually tiring for everyone on earth

indicators.note: unusually means arranged in an odd way, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: U is the British film rating for universal, suitable for all

explanation.surface: A puzzle that is strangely tiring for all people on the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrigue is to puzzle or fascinate, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Fixed jailbird's meeting with good man, social worker

parts.note: a con (convict) is a jailbird; the 's adds S
ST, saint, a good man
an ant is a social insect that works

explanation.surface: A prisoner's meeting with a good man and a social worker is arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a care professional but the worker ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant and fixed both mean unchanging, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Regular claim in court

indicators.note: in puts the claim inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: a lien is a legal claim on property

explanation.surface: A routine legal claim made in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a habitual customer, as is a client.

clue.text: Call round in pursuit of a cold tart

indicators.note: in pursuit of means following, so this piece comes after the others
round means turned around, read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to call or summon

explanation.surface: Call round after a cold dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like a pastry but is the adjective meaning sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic means like vinegar, sour, the same as sharp-tasting.

clue.text: Did recruit make appreciative noises over pithead now and then?

indicators.note: over in a down clue means placed above the following piece

parts.note: to coo is to murmur admiringly

indicators.note: now and then means occasionally, taking alternate letters of pithead

explanation.surface: A mining recruit makes admiring sounds over the pit's top now and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of pithead give PTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To co-opt someone is to bring them into a group, past tense matching 'did recruit'.

clue.text: Pub reportedly having top-notch ham

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word is taken for how it sounds

parts.note: an inn is a pub
expert means first-rate, highly skilled

explanation.surface: A pub said to serve top-quality ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' is not the meat but an unskilled performer or amateur.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is clumsy or amateurish, hence unskilled; adjective use of the word.

clue.text: Flowers in bunches by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it signals the word is chosen for how it is pronounced

parts.note: flocks are groups or bunches, of birds or people

explanation.surface: Flowers gathered in bunches, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlox is a garden plant with clusters of bright blooms; the name is both singular and plural.

clue.text: Went dizzy between rounds getting quick punches

indicators.note: between means set inside, between the two circles

parts.note: two round letters, O and O

indicators.note: dizzy means in a spin, so the letters of went are mixed

explanation.surface: A boxer went giddy between rounds after taking rapid blows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' looks like boxing rounds but stands for two ring-shaped letters O.
explanation.definitionFit: In boxing, a rapid pair of blows from left then right is the classic combination.

clue.text: Take sides with clear opinion

indicators.note: sides means the outer letters of take

parts.note: net, as in net profit, means clear after deductions

explanation.surface: Pick a side and voice a clear view.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held, akin to a held view.

clue.text: Hit back causing swelling

indicators.note: back means the word is turned round

parts.note: to tonk is to hit hard, an informal British word

explanation.surface: Retaliation leading to a bump.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot can be a lump or swelling, as in a muscle or wood.

clue.text: New Saab losing rear end crashed by learner — it's to do with the hooter

definitions.text: it's to do with the hooter

indicators.note: crashed means wrecked, so the letters are jumbled
losing rear end means the last letter of the car name is dropped

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A new Saab missing its back end has been crashed by a learner driver who sounded the horn.
explanation.walkthrough: N plus SAA rearranged gives NASA; 'hooter' is slang for nose, not a car horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means relating to the nose, which is slangily called a hooter.

clue.text: Fred's partner given fruitcake and biscuit

parts.note: Ginger Rogers danced with Fred Astaire
a fruitcake is slang for an eccentric person, a nut

explanation.surface: Fred Astaire's dance partner is handed cake and a cookie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruitcake' is slang for a crazy person; a gingernut is a hard British ginger biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard ginger-flavoured cookie popular in Britain is one kind of biscuit.

clue.text: Anticipated accepting nothing traitor coughed up

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: expected means anticipated
O is zero, nothing
a rat is a betrayer

explanation.surface: The traitor was expected to pay up, having been given nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coughed up' looks like paying out but means spat out literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To expectorate is to bring up phlegm from the chest, past tense matching.
